cohort.definition: Students and recent graduates entering Microsoft in software engineering, anchored on the firm's published Explore program listing for early-year undergraduates and its university recruiting pages. Experienced hires are a separate cohort.
cohort.time_window: listings and program pages live when checked, October 2026

data_sources.label: Microsoft official Explore program listing (via University of Washington careers mirror of the Microsoft posting) — required and preferred qualifications, pay range and application window

entries.label: No school pattern published
entries.note: Microsoft publishes no school distribution for its hires, and the Explore listing names no schools. This record states no school pattern rather than guessing one.

entries.label: No prior employer required at the earliest door
entries.note: The Explore listing's screen is coursework-based (introductory CS and calculus), not employer-based — a stated screen, not a measured employer mix.

entries.label: Computer science, computer engineering, software engineering or a related technical major
entries.note: Named as the preferred field of study in the Explore listing — a stated preference, not a measured major mix of hires.

entries.label: Programming fundamentals and problem solving
entries.note: The Explore listing centers hands-on work with software development tools and programming languages alongside a manager and mentors — a stated environment, not a measured skill mix.

path_patterns.pattern: Explore first: the early-years program rotates across engineering, product and program roles before students specialize
University internship, then convert: interns must be returning to school for a full academic term after the internship

entry_routes.accessibility_note: The published earliest door: second-year enrollment at application, introductory CS and one term of calculus completed by program start.
Enrollment in a relevant bachelor's, master's, MBA or PhD program in the term before the internship, returning to school afterwards.

entry_routes.route: New-graduate roles via Microsoft Careers students pages
entry_routes.accessibility_note: The students and graduates section of Microsoft Careers is the live source for full-time entry postings.

hiring_bar_summary.statement: Microsoft's published Explore bar: currently pursuing a full-time bachelor's degree, enrolled in the second year of a four-year program at application, with an introductory computer science course and one semester of calculus completed by the start of the program; demonstrated interest in a technical major is preferred.

stated.statement: Required: full-time bachelor's enrollment and second-year standing at application for Explore; introductory CS and one semester of calculus by program start.
For university internships generally: enrollment in a relevant degree program in the term immediately before the internship and a return to school for one full academic term afterwards.

revealed.statement: Revealed by Microsoft's own student interview guidance: the process aims to discover what candidates have learned in school, evaluate critical thinking, assess problem solving and measure ability to learn — learnability is screened as a first-class signal.

process_stages.description: Apply against a listing whose required and preferred qualifications are published in full; Microsoft states it accepts applications and processes offers on an ongoing basis through the academic calendar for these roles.

interview_styles.statement: Microsoft's student interview guidance states the process aims to discover what you have learned in school, evaluate critical thinking, assess how you solve problems and measure your ability to learn. This record found no official page detailing exact round counts, and invents none.

values_culture_signals.statement: The Explore listing frames the work as building on values of respect, integrity and accountability to create a culture of inclusion — stated in the posting itself, not just marketing pages.

hiring_cadence.statement: The Explore listing states Microsoft accepts applications and processes offers for these roles on an ongoing basis throughout the academic calendar. Listings open and close by team, so the careers site is the live source of truth.

compensation_notes.statement: Microsoft publishes pay information for interns on its official intern pay page and states a base pay range on the Explore listing itself, with location-specific ranges for higher-cost areas. This record quotes no figure of its own: the listing and the pay page are the authoritative sources for a given role's terms.

referral_weight_notes.statement: No official statement on referral weight appears in the sources checked. The published screens are coursework- and evidence-based, so a referral may open a conversation but the stated qualifications still carry the decision.

red_flags.statement: Microsoft's program rules state candidates cannot complete back-to-back internships and cannot take classes while interning — plan academic calendars around that term, not around hope.
Explore is location-specific in the listing checked (Redmond-based); other offices run through the general careers site, so a single listing never describes the whole map.

thesis_text: Microsoft publishes its earliest door plainly: the Explore program is built for students in the first years of a bachelor's degree who have finished an introductory computer science course and a term of calculus, rotating across software engineering, product management and technical program management. Beyond that door, university internships ask for enrollment in a relevant degree and a return to school after the internship. The revealed tilt is learnability — the firm's own interview guidance for students says it tests what you have learned, how you think through problems, and how fast you learn. No population data on who gets in is published, so this record is qualitative throughout and states no school or major shares.
known_biases_of_data: No population sample exists for this record: Microsoft publishes requirements, not who passes them. Every distribution restates the published screen qualitatively.
A job listing is the firm's stated ideal; it understates how much referrals and school recruiting presence may matter in practice, which public sources cannot measure.
The Explore listing checked describes one program in one office; team and regional listings vary.
schema_normalized: Envelope mapped to the 125-career-intel validator schema by scripts/career/normalize-cir.py. No facts added, removed, or altered.
